title: platform-sprint-blitz-all-hands-briefing-feb-26-2026
content: Purpose: quick-read notes for the Feb 26 platform sprint-blitz + all-hands. This was a compact town-hall for cross-org alignment on the next 6 weeks of work (focus: capacity, rollout safety, and low-latency wins). Attendees: ~40 eng (platform, serving-runtime, infra), PMs for Dedicated & Private, SRE reps, Solutions Eng. Opening (Priya): context and ask - we need predictable capacity for Dedicated Q2 sales commitments; quick wins are: 1) reduce p90 tail by 20% via kernel fallback, 2) unblock a canary rollout for quantized 7B variants, 3) finalize autoscaler policy for burst lanes. High-level metrics snapshot (Samir): - Prod token throughput: 1.2B/day (up 8% w/w) - 99th pct latency (text gen): 780ms (regional skew in eu-west) - Error rate: 0.7% (RPC timeout hotspots on gpu-2 nodes) Notes / Decisions: - Fallback kernel feature: greenlight to ship experimental fallback in canary by Mar 12. Owner: Ethan. QA: add synthetic workload that reproduces 99pct tails (JIRA-PLAT-1129). - Canary for quantized 7B: approved for limited customers; rollout gating criteria: quality regression <2% on eval set + observability hooks enabled. Owner: Marta. - Autoscaler burst lanes: adopt conservative burst threshold (20% extra) and enable manual override during sales demos. Action: infra to run a 72-hour soak in staging before enabling in prod. - KV-cache eviction behavior: revert the recent aggressive eviction change; implement soft-evict and metric tagging by Mar 5. Owner: Samir. Cross-org asks to Serving Runtime: - Please prioritize trace-level context propagation for fallback hops (needed for observability and accurate cost attribution). Slack thread: #serving-runtime-fallbacks. - Add token-cost header to streaming responses (PR link in linked_artifacts). Risk / Open issues: - Capacity math for Dedicated: current quota model underestimates burst usage for mixed-seq workloads. Platform to propose a revised formula by Mar 4. - Observability retention costs: proposal to tier retention per customer is blocked by billing integration work. Need finance + product sync. Action Items (concise): - Ethan: synthetic tail test harness + JIRA-PLAT-1129 (by Mar 3) - Marta: canary rollout plan + eval checklist (by Mar 8) - Samir: KV-cache soft-evict RFC + perf benchmarks (by Mar 5) - Infra (Alicia): staging soak for burst lanes (start Mar 1, report Mar 6) - Product (Jon): updated Dedicated capacity pricing / quota formula draft (by Mar 4) Communication plan: - Short recap email to eng-all within 24h (Priya) - Dedicated customers impacted by canary will receive notice 48h prior to opt-in (Solutions Eng). Notes-to-self / friction points (informal): - Several participants asked for clearer SLAs vs SLOs doc; follow-up doc to clarify wording (SLA vs SLO) is required. - We need better pre-rollout checklist: include perf-run, observability hooks, and rollback playbook. - Heard concerns about on-call cognitive load when fallback triggers; idea: temporary runbook + on-call rotation for high-impact rollouts. Misc tech snippets captured during discussion: - Benchmark snippet: "--seq 1024 --batch 16 --kv-cache off" produced best p90 for fallback test on a100-80. - Suggested default memory-quantization table (draft): 8-bit-per-tensor for non-attention weights, 4-bit for feed-forward in 7B if accuracy checks pass. Follow-ups scheduled: - Deep-dive with Serving Runtime on fallback kernels (Mar 3, 60m) - Platform perf retro (Mar 11, 90m) - Cross-functional rollout rehearsal (Mar 9, 120m, staging) Links mentioned: Confluence PLAT-423 (capacity model), JIRA-PLAT-1129 (tail test), GH PR 987 (token-cost header). Closing notes: tone was pragmatic — focus on measurable rollouts and short soak windows rather than big-bang launches. Keep sprint-blitz format: short synchronous updates + clear owner list. If you weren’t at the meeting and are assigned an action, please ping the owner on the linked jira or Slack thread and add any blockers to the ticket.
